nodes.label: Streamlit app (app.py + pages/)
nodes.rationale: Described as the complete, feature-rich product today — every feature in the guide runs there; kept as the recommended interface while the newer app is unfinished.

nodes.label: FastAPI + React app (backend/ + frontend/)
nodes.rationale: Under active construction: the API works but the browser UI is still a visual shell not yet wired to real conversations, so the guide tells users to use Streamlit instead.

nodes.label: Why this app exists (the business case)
nodes.norm_label: why this app exists (the business case)

nodes.label: Local-first (promise)
nodes.rationale: Runs against the user's own Ollama install by default; nothing leaves the machine unless a cloud provider is explicitly enabled. No subscription required for a usable assistant.

nodes.label: Zero-maintenance (promise)
nodes.rationale: Model lists are fetched live every time, so a newly pulled Ollama model appears after a refresh with no code/config edits.

nodes.label: It knows you (promise)
nodes.rationale: Long-term memory and a personalization profile are built from conversations so answers get more relevant over time without the user managing a prompt library by hand.

nodes.label: Who it's for
nodes.rationale: Targets privacy-conscious individuals, developers wanting side-by-side model comparison, and teams evaluating multiple LLM providers without committing to one vendor or paying recurring cost beyond chosen provider keys.

nodes.label: Clone, set up, and run it
nodes.norm_label: clone, set up, and run it

nodes.label: Privacy and security, in plain terms
nodes.rationale: Keys never touch disk and live only in server memory for the session; local stays local by default (SQLite + ChromaDB in data/, no telemetry); cloud use sends message + attached context to that provider same as pasting into their own UI.
nodes.norm_label: privacy and security, in plain terms

nodes.label: Two-applications parity-migration mental model
nodes.rationale: Treating the repo as one UI with two equivalent implementations would be misleading; the legacy Streamlit app is the complete end-user product today, v2 FastAPI/React is a functional backend behind an unwired shell - modeling it as a parity migration sets correct expectations for contributors.

nodes.label: Cooperative run cancellation
nodes.rationale: Cancellation is cooperative (a threading event checked between streamed chunks) rather than a hard interrupt, because a provider stream can't be preempted mid-network-call - so a provider stalled before yielding cannot be interrupted immediately.

nodes.norm_label: zero-to-hero study handbook, legacy v1 (pdf, streamlit-only)

nodes.label: Event-driven UI with Streamlit reruns
nodes.rationale: Streamlit reruns the whole script on interaction; st.session_state, st.fragment(run_every=...), and callbacks are used to keep state consistent while rendering live updates without a client-side framework.

nodes.label: Background worker pattern (daemon threads + Job registry)
nodes.rationale: Long-running generation runs in daemon threads via a process-global Job registry (src/jobs.py) so the Streamlit UI thread stays responsive during streaming, OCR, or web search.
nodes.norm_label: background worker pattern (daemon threads + job registry)

nodes.label: Functional module style with typed data carriers
nodes.rationale: Most logic is organized as module-level functions with small dataclasses for structured data (ModelInfo, ApiModel, SelectedModel, Attachment, Job) rather than classes/services, keeping the codebase flat and easy to trace.
nodes.norm_label: functional module style with typed data carriers
